en: Points of Controversy Great Fifty-Section Fourteenth Chapter
The Discourse on Noble Form:
Is noble form derived from the great elements? Yes.
Is noble form wholesome?
Yes. Are the great elements wholesome? No.
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Are the great elements (mahābhūta) indeterminate (abyākata)? Yes.
Is noble form indeterminate?
One should not say so … [and so on] … Is noble form derived from the great elements?
“Yes.

“Is noble form (ariyarūpa) without taints (anāsava), not subject to fetters, not subject to ties, not subject to floods, not subject to yokes, not subject to hindrances, unclung-to, not subject to clinging, and not subject to defilement?
“Yes.”
Are the great elements (mahābhūta) without taints (anāsava)? ... [and so on] ... not subject to defilement (asaṅkilesika)?
One should not say so. ... [and so on] ...
Are the great elements with taints (sāsava), subject to fetters (saṃyojaniya), ... [and so on] ... subject to defilement (saṅkilesika)?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Then is noble form (ariyarūpa) subject to the taints (sāsava), subject to the fetters (saṃyojaniya), and subject to defilement (saṅkilesiya)?
You must not say so … [and so on] … No, indeed.
Is it not to be said that noble form is derived from the great elements?
Yes, it is.
But was it not said by the Blessed One:
“Bhikkhus, whatever form there is, all that is the four great elements and the form derived from the four great elements”?
Is this indeed a sutta?
“Yes,” he replied.
“In that case, noble form is derived from the great elements.
The Discussion on Noble Form is finished.
